title: Empirical kernel cost index and online repartitioner for sequence-distribution aware kernel routing
creator: Asha Patel
description: Problem: The current kernel selection layer uses static heuristics calibrated from offline microbenchmarks. We see tail latency and cost regressions on customer traffic with bimodal and long-tail sequence-length distributions (chat prefill heavy vs short-query decode). Goal: design an empirical, low-overhead kernel cost index (KCI) that captures real-time latency and throughput trade-offs per model-variant + hardware slot and an online repartitioner that routes requests to kernel implementation tiers based on observed sequence-length distribution and KCI. This ticket covers design, prototype, wall-clock experiments, and rollout plan for Canary in runtime-1.20.
acceptance_criteria: KCI computation implemented in runtime (profiling window <= 10s) and exposed via existing metrics pipeline (Prometheus labels: model, variant, gpu_type, kernel_impl)
Online repartitioner correctly switches kernel_impl tiers for >= 3 target percentiles (P50/P90/P99) without violating latency SLO on a synthetic bimodal workload
End-to-end PR with unit + integration tests merged; canary rollout plan documented with rollback criteria and runbook
Cost delta (tokens/sec * $/token proxy) measured and documented for three representative workloads showing >= 8% cost reduction or improved latency headroom for same cost
tasks: Design KCI: formula candidates (latency-weighted cost, throughput-normalized latency, tokenized CPU/GPU cycles estimate)
Add lightweight tracer to measure per-request kernel_impl timing and emit KCI inputs (latency, decode tokens, gpu_util snapshot)
Implement sliding-window KCI aggregator with decay and jitter guardrails
Integrate KCI into routing layer and add a safe-tiered repartitioner (fast, balanced, low-cost) with hysteresis and minimum dwell time
Create perf harness: synthetic bimodal seqlen generator and record suite for P50/P90/P99 and cost metrics
Run experiment matrix across 3 models (llama-13b, redwood-7b-quant, open-evm-6b) on A100 and L40 hardware
Analyze results, pick initial thresholds, prepare canary config and rollout plan
Docs: runtime README + operator runbook + dashboard panels for KCI and repartitioner decisions
PR: code + tests + benchmark results attached
comments: 2026-02-12 - Asha Patel: Kickoff meeting notes attached in Drive (link: https://drive.company/redwood/runtime/kci-kickoff). Decided to prioritize minimum runtime overhead (<1% CPU) and deterministic hysteresis policies over aggressive ML-based routing for v1.
